scenes.heading: Shape of data distributions
scenes.say: Two classes can have the same average mark but completely different results. The shape of the data tells you the real story.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A slide: a tall ladder, then a long gentle slope
scenes.science: Data: a big pile of values, then a long thin tail
scenes.breaks: A slide has one high point; some data sets have two peaks, or none.
scenes.say: Picture a playground slide from the side: a tall ladder at one end and a long gentle slope at the other. Data often looks like that, with a big pile of values and a long thin tail. We name the shape after the direction the tail points.

scenes.heading: Positively skewed: tail to the right
notes: A long tail stretches right to 6
scenes.say: Here's how many pets people own. First the tall bars on the left: most people have zero or one pet. Then the bars get lower and lower, out to six pets. The tail points right, towards the bigger numbers, so this is positively skewed.

scenes.heading: Negatively skewed: tail to the left
notes: A long tail stretches left to 30%
scenes.say: Now marks on an easy test. Most bars are tall at the high end, from seventy to one hundred percent. The tail stretches left, down to thirty. A tail to the left means negatively skewed.
scenes.caption: Now marks on an easy test. Most bars are tall at the high end, from 70 to 100%. The tail stretches left, down to 30%. A tail to the left means negatively skewed.

scenes.heading: Where does the mean go?
scenes.say: The tail drags the mean towards it, but the median hardly moves. So with a positive skew the mean is bigger than the median, and with a negative skew the mean is smaller. In a symmetric shape, they're about equal.

scenes.heading: Check the shape with numbers
scenes.question: Homework minutes: 11, 12, 12, 13, 14, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 23, 27, 34, 45
scenes.say: Fourteen students' homework times have a tail out to forty-five minutes, so they're positively skewed. The mean is two hundred and seventy-five divided by fourteen, about nineteen point six. The median is the average of fifteen and sixteen, fifteen point five. The mean is bigger, just as the shape predicts.
scenes.caption: These homework times have a tail out to 45 minutes: positively skewed. Mean = 275 ÷ 14 ≈ 19.6. Median = (15 + 16) ÷ 2 = 15.5. The mean is bigger, as the shape predicts.

scenes.heading: Other features to describe
points: Bimodal: two peaks, often two groups mixed
Outlier: a value far from the rest
Gap: a stretch with no values
scenes.say: Also look for other features. Two peaks means bimodal, often two groups mixed together. An outlier is a value far from the rest. A cluster is a bunch of values close together, and a gap is a stretch with no values at all.

points: Tail right = positive; tail left = negative
scenes.say: Quick recap. The tail tells the tale: tail right is positive skew, tail left is negative. The mean follows the tail. Two peaks means bimodal. And always mention outliers, clusters and gaps. Now try the practice questions!
